The target server is running RHEL 8.10 .Based on our assessment, the feasibility and recommendations are as below:
1. Container & Runtime Tools
  • Podman:
    Feasible and recommended. Podman is natively supported on RHEL 8 and compliant with hardened environments.
  • Docker & Docker Compose:
    Unfeasible. Docker requires an external vendor repository and runs a privileged daemon, which is not Red Hat–supported on RHEL 8. It will impact the production server.
 
  • Please Note-  Podman is the preferred alternative.
2. Programming Languages & SDKs
  • Python 3, pip3: Feasible and supported.
Recommended - java-11-openjdk.x86_64 / java-1.8.0-openjdk.x86_64
 
  • Python 2, pip: Not recommended as Python 2 is EOL.  
 
  • Java (JRE/JVM) & Java SDK (JDK):
    Feasible using Red Hat–supported OpenJDK packages.
    Java 11 (LTS) is recommended for production use.
  • JavaM / JavaSDK: Covered under OpenJDK Runtime and OpenJDK‑devel packages respectively.
3. Web, Middleware & Storage Components
  • Nginx: Feasible via AppStream repositories.
  • Redis CLI: Feasible (client tools only). Redis server service will remain disabled.
  • MinIO: Feasible (binary-based deployment), subject to port and access approval.
4. Cloud, Security & Networking Utilities
  • AWS CLI (v2): Feasible and recommended. Installed as a self‑contained binary without Python dependency.
  • OpenSSL, curl, netstat, traceroute, ss, nslookup: Feasible (available via BaseOS).
  • vim, vi, tree: Feasible.
 
5. Overall Recommendation
All requested tools are largely feasible on RHEL 8.10. However:
  • Podman should be used instead of Docker wherever possible.
  • Python 2 usage is discouraged due to EOL status.
  • Docker installation should proceed only after security clearance.
Storage will be SAN backed filesystem and separate mount point will be provided after LLD discussion.
 
We request you to take up with the security team for any security clearance and arrange a LLD discussion with all the stake holders to proceed further.

system.cpu.percent Usage above 80% indicates CPU saturation and potential performance issues. Below 5% means the CPU is mostly idle, which is normal during off-peak times.

To fix this:

results.description:
Minutes of Meeting (MoM)
Meeting Title: Discussion on VKYC Call Connection Issues and Analytics Observations
Date: 17 June 2026
Time: 12:33 PM IST
Platform: Teams
Attendees:
  • Dnyaneshwar Shekade – Application Support Engineer L2, Think360.ai
  • Yashuman Shekar
  • Shreya Singh ( Application owner) 
Objective
To discuss the major reasons behind customer call connection failures in the VKYC journey, understand rejection scenarios related to customer data mismatches, review OTP failure cases, and identify discrepancies in analytics reporting.
Discussion Points
1. Call Not Connected Issues
The team discussed multiple scenarios that contribute to the "Call Not Connected" issue during the VKYC process.
Scenario 1: Customer's Slow Internet Connectivity
  • Customers with poor or unstable internet connections are unable to establish a successful connection with the VKYC agent.
  • Due to network latency and packet loss, the call initiation process fails before the video session is established.
  • This results in the session being categorized as Call Not Connected.
Observation:
Poor internet connectivity on the customer's end is one of the primary reasons for call failures.
Scenario 2: User Socket Disconnection
  • In several cases, the customer's internet connection drops during the session initiation process.
  • Because of the unstable network, the WebSocket connection gets disconnected.
  • Once the socket is disconnected, the signaling process fails and the call cannot be established successfully.
Observation:
Socket disconnection due to intermittent internet connectivity is another significant contributor to call connection failures.
Scenario 3: Customer Waiting in Queue and Agent Unavailability
The following sequence was discussed:
  1. Customer enters the VKYC queue and waits for agent allocation.
  2. At that time, the available agent is already engaged on another call.
  3. The customer remains in the waiting queue until the agent becomes available.
  4. During the waiting period, many customers:
    • Exit the VKYC page,
    • Switch browser tabs,
    • Minimize the application,
    • Navigate away from the session page.
  5. By the time an agent becomes available and attempts to connect, the customer is no longer actively present on the VKYC page.
Result:
The call fails to establish and is marked as Call Not Connected.
Observation:
Customer inactivity while waiting in the queue is a major contributor to the overall call connection failure percentage.
2. Customer Data Mismatch Cases
The discussion then moved to cases involving customer information mismatches, particularly economic details.
Example Scenario
  • Customer enters Annual Income as:
    • ₹5 Lakhs in the application form.
  • During the VKYC verification call, the customer verbally states:
    • ₹6 Lakhs or ₹7 Lakhs.
In such situations:
  1. The VKYC agent asks the customer for reconfirmation.
  2. The agent attempts to validate the information again.
  3. If the customer fails to provide consistent or accurate information, the verification cannot proceed.
Result:
The application gets rejected due to a Data Mismatch.
Observation:
Economic data discrepancies, especially annual income declarations, are one of the major reasons for customer rejections.
3. OTP Failed Cases
The team discussed the cases categorized as OTP Failed.
Current Understanding
  • During the standard VKYC journey, there is no OTP verification step being performed by the VKYC application.
  • Instead, customers are presented with security questions where they are required to repeat or provide a four-digit verification number.
  • This process does not constitute an OTP validation mechanism.
Concern Raised
Since there is no OTP step in the current VKYC workflow:
  • The reason behind sessions being categorized as OTP Failed remains unclear.
  • The support team currently does not have sufficient information to determine the source of this status.
Requirement from Stakeholders
The team requested:
  • Response JSON payloads,
  • Webhook responses,
  • Any upstream integration responses,
that explicitly indicates why sessions are being marked under the OTP Failed category.
Action Required:
The respective team is requested to share the response payloads and integration details for further analysis.
4. Analytics Discrepancy Identified
While investigating the Call Not Connected cases, another observation was made.
Observation
Certain sessions:
  1. Successfully connected with agents.
  2. Proceeded further in the VKYC journey.
  3. Eventually got rejected.
However, these same sessions are still appearing in the Analytics dashboard under:
"Call Never Accepted"
Impact
This indicates a possible discrepancy between:
  • Actual call state transitions, and
  • Analytics event reporting.

Regards,
Dnyaneshwar Shekade
L2 Tech Support Engineer (KwikID), Think360.ai
Dnyaneshwar.Shekade@think360.ai
